verdict: Coinbase's revenue jumped 55% from a year ago to $1.87B as crypto trading rebounded, and net income rose nearly six-fold to $433M — a $424M paper gain on the crypto it holds as an investment more than covered roughly $400M of paper losses on its other investments.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago — crypto markets rebounded

kpis.label: $USD resources
kpis.note: cash, USDC and investments — up 28% in the quarter

segments.name: Transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees from crypto trading — consumer $844M, institutional $135M, other $68M. Trading rebounded as crypto prices rose; revenue was up 37% from Q2.

segments.name: Subscription and services
segments.note: Steadier income: stablecoin revenue $355M, blockchain rewards $185M, interest and finance fees $65M, and other services $143M.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Interest earned on Coinbase's own corporate cash.

opex.name: Technology & development
opex.note: Building the platform — engineering and product, now including Deribit, the options exchange Coinbase bought in August 2025.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — legal, compliance and the back office.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising, USDC rewards and winning customers.

opex.name: Other operating expense, net
opex.note: $61M of other operating costs — mostly customer reimbursements and legal costs from the May 2025 data-theft incident — partly offset by a $36M paper gain on crypto Coinbase holds to run its business.

follow100Note: Of every $100 Coinbase took in, paper gains on the crypto it holds as an investment added $22.68, while paper losses on its strategic investments took $20.36 back out — the two nearly cancelled. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Trading roared back
takeaways.text: Transaction revenue rose 83% year over year to $1.05B — consumer trading alone was $844M — as crypto prices and volumes recovered from a soft second quarter.

takeaways.title: Paper gains beat paper losses
takeaways.text: The crypto Coinbase holds as an investment gained $424M on paper, while its strategic investments lost about $400M. Adjusted net income was $421M — close to the reported $433M, because the two swings nearly cancelled.

takeaways.title: Data-theft costs lingered
takeaways.text: Other operating costs included $61M tied to the May 2025 data-theft incident — voluntary customer reimbursements and legal costs. Coinbase also closed its Deribit acquisition in August, adding costs across its main expense lines.

oneTimers: A $424M mark-to-market gain on crypto assets held for investment — non-cash, and it reverses if crypto prices fall.
About $400M of net losses on strategic and other investments, inside the $381M of other expense, net.
$61M of costs from the May 2025 data-theft incident — customer reimbursements and legal bills — inside other operating expense.
otherDetail: A $424M paper gain on crypto Coinbase holds as an investment, less $381M of other expense — mostly losses on strategic investments — and $22M of interest expense: a net $22M.
footerNote: Coinbase reports no gross-profit line; 'Transaction expense' — the direct cost of processing trades — is shown as cost of revenue. 'Other operating expense, net' of $26M nets a $36M gain on crypto held for operations against $61M of other operating costs, most of it data-theft incident costs. Figures are from Coinbase's Q3 2025 shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-Q.
